pairs.title: Conformal constraint weights and charged time-symmetric data

A.title: Conformal electrovacuum seeds
A.statement: On an oriented smooth Riemannian three-manifold fix a smooth seed metric hbar, divergence-free vector fields Ebar,Bbar, a positive smooth function psi and constants Lambda and tau. Set h=psi^4 hbar, E=psi^-6 Ebar, B=psi^-6 Bbar, and K=(tau/3)h+psi^-2 Abar with Abar trace free. E,B are geometric-normalized fields, not SI fields.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Exact conformal electrovacuum constraint transformation
A.statement: With the stated seed, div_h E=psi^-6 div_hbar Ebar and similarly for B. The Hamiltonian constraint is -8 Delta_bar psi+Rbar psi-|Abar|^2 psi^-7+(2 tau^2/3-2 Lambda)psi^5-2(|Ebar|^2+|Bbar|^2)psi^-3=0. The momentum equation remains a separate constraint; when K=0 and Ebar cross Bbar=0 it holds identically.
A.proof_route: Differentiate sqrt(det h)=psi^6 sqrt(det hbar); contract the connection difference C^k_ij=2psi^-1(delta^k_i psi_j+delta^k_j psi_i-hbar_ij psi^k) to obtain R(h)=psi^-5(-8 Delta_bar psi+Rbar psi). Substitute trace and norm weights; no elliptic existence is inferred.

A.title: RN conformal data on a punctured exterior
A.statement: For r>0, psi^2=(1+m/(2r))^2-q^2/(4r^2)>0, Ebar=q r^-2 partial_r, Bbar=0 and K=0 satisfy the Lambda=0 constraints. For m>|q|, r=(sqrt(m^2-q^2))/2 is a minimal sphere and R_areal=r psi^2=m+sqrt(m^2-q^2); no global event-horizon claim is included.
A.proof_route: Differentiate the displayed radial function in Delta psi=psi_rr+2psi_r/r and verify the Hamiltonian equation; divergence of q r^-2 partial_r vanishes on r>0. Differentiate r psi^2, and use area=4pi R_areal^2 and the conformal normal to check minimality.

B.title: Extremal cylindrical end
B.statement: For m=|q|>0 the above psi^2=1+m/r has areal radius r+m, no positive-r minimal sphere, and an infinite proper-distance end as r tends to zero.
B.proof_route: Integrate psi^2 dr=(1+m/r)dr and differentiate r+m.

B.title: Unscaled vector fields fail the transformed Gauss law
B.statement: On a Euclidean patch with nonconstant positive psi and constant Ebar, setting E=Ebar rather than psi^-6 Ebar generally gives div_h E=6 Ebar(log psi), which need not vanish.
B.proof_route: Choose psi=exp(x), Ebar=partial_x and compute the volume divergence.

pairs.title: Local nonlinear constraint construction with explicit analytic obligations

A.title: Bounded-domain charged conformal problem
A.statement: Let Omega be a bounded connected smooth domain in R^3, 0<alpha<1, S a nonnegative C^{0,alpha} function and epsilon real. Seek psi=1+u, u in C^{2,alpha}(closure Omega), u=0 on boundary, satisfying -8 Delta psi=2 epsilon^2 S psi^-3 and psi>0. This is the time-symmetric flat-seed Lambda=0 Hamiltonian problem; divergence-free parallel Ebar,Bbar giving S must be supplied independently.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Dirichlet Hölder inverse required by the constraint branch
A.statement: For a bounded smooth Omega and 0<alpha<1, -Delta:C^{2,alpha}(closure Omega) intersect C_0(closure Omega) to C^{0,alpha}(closure Omega) is a bounded linear isomorphism. The zero subscript here means zero boundary trace, not compact support.
A.proof_route: New local authoring obligation: construct a weak H_0^1 solution by Poincare plus Lax–Milgram; prove the boundary Schauder estimate by flattening finitely many boundary charts, the constant-coefficient Newtonian-potential Hölder estimate and reflection/localization, then a continuation argument. Poincare, trace/density, boundary flattening and the Hölder kernel estimate must be fully proved in this lemma or split into same-page suppliers before dispatch. No blanket use of a citation or a mere H^2 regularity supplier suffices.

A.title: Local Banach implicit-function supplier
A.statement: For Banach X,Y, a C^1 map F on a neighborhood of (0,0) in X times R with F(0,0)=0 and D_xF(0,0) boundedly invertible has a unique nearby C^1 solution branch x(epsilon). The derivative formula is x_prime=-D_xF^-1 D_epsilonF.
A.proof_route: Prove by a uniform contraction x -> x-L^-1 F(x,epsilon) on a small closed ball, using continuity of D_xF and the fundamental theorem along line segments; differentiability follows from the difference quotient and the inverse Neumann series. Apply the exact published contraction theorem to the nonempty complete closed ball; the operator inverse and differentiability steps are proved locally.

A.title: Small charged Dirichlet conformal branch
A.statement: The bounded-domain problem has a unique branch in a fixed C^{2,alpha} neighborhood of psi=1 for sufficiently small absolute epsilon, with psi>=1 and psi-1=epsilon^2 v+O(epsilon^4), where -8 Delta v=2S and v has zero boundary value. Uniqueness is local, not a global conformal-method theorem.
A.proof_route: Use F(u,e)=-8Delta u-2e^2 S(1+u)^-3; its derivative at zero is -8Delta. Restrict ||u||_infinity<1/2. Smoothness of scalar inverse powers gives a smooth Banach map. The maximum principle is proved at an interior negative minimum and by the weak comparison argument; Taylor expand in e^2 and use the inverse bound to obtain the remainder.

B.title: Small constant electric seed in a ball
B.statement: A constant Ebar and Bbar=0 on a smooth ball give S=|Ebar|^2 and the local theorem constructs smooth positive constrained time-symmetric data there. Boundary data are prescribed mathematical data, not an isolated asymptotically flat black hole.
B.proof_route: Constant fields have zero divergence and cross product; elliptic bootstrapping for smooth S is a further same-lemma estimate.

pairs.title: Spherical electrovacuum mass and local rigidity

A.title: Spherical orbit geometry and charged mass
A.statement: On U times S^2 let g=g2+r^2 gamma with g2 Lorentzian, r>0 smooth, and F=(q_e/r^2)vol_g2+q_m omega_S2 with fixed product orientation. Define Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2 and varpi=(r/2)(1-g2^-1(dr,dr))+Q^2/(2r)-Lambda r^3/6. Constants q_e,q_m are signed fluxes in the chosen orientation.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Warped two-sphere curvature equations
A.statement: For the spherical ansatz, Ric_AB=Ric(g2)_AB-2r^-1 Hess_AB r and Ric_ij=[1-|dr|^2-r Box_g2 r] gamma_ij; mixed entries vanish. In electrovacuum Hess r is pure trace and d varpi=0.
A.proof_route: Compute Gamma^i_Aj=r^-1 partial_A r delta^i_j and Gamma^A_ij=-r partial^A r gamma_ij, insert into all Ricci slots and use Ric(g2)=(R2/2)g2. Maxwell implies constant sphere fluxes; substitute Ric=Lambda g+2Q(F) and differentiate the displayed varpi, cancelling dr coefficients.

A.title: Local RN-(A)dS rigidity away from critical areal gradients
A.statement: On a simply connected electrovacuum quotient patch where dr is nonzero and g2^-1(dr,dr) is nowhere zero, varpi=m is constant and the metric is locally RN-(A)dS with f(r)=1-2m/r+Q^2/r^2-Lambda r^2/3. The causal character of the Killing coordinate follows the sign of f. Constant-radius solutions and null-gradient patches are outside this statement.
A.proof_route: The rotated gradient X=*2 dr is Killing because Hess r is pure trace. It preserves r and commutes with dr/f; integrate their two commuting nonzero fields to quotient coordinates. Normalize their constant scale and use |dr|^2=f from varpi=m to obtain -f dt^2+f^-1 dr^2. No analytic extension or global uniqueness is inferred.

B.title: Bertotti–Robinson excluded by dr nonzero
B.statement: The constant-radius electrovacuum product has dr=0 and cannot be represented by the theorem using r as a coordinate, despite solving the same electrovacuum equations.
B.proof_route: Its area radius is constant; a coordinate function has nonzero differential.

pairs.title: Charged photon trapping and extremal scaling

A.title: RN circular null radii and exterior instability
A.statement: For asymptotically flat RN with m>0 and 0<=Q^2<m^2, the outer circular null radius is (3m+sqrt(9m^2-8Q^2))/2 and lies strictly above r_plus=m+sqrt(m^2-Q^2). It is a strict local maximum of f/r^2.
A.proof_route: Conserve E=f t_dot and L=r^2 phi_dot in an equatorial geodesic; r_dot^2+L^2 f/r^2=E^2. Differentiate f/r^2=-2(r^2-3mr+2Q^2)/r^5 after one derivative; solve the quadratic and use its positive discriminant to determine the second derivative sign. Compare outer radius to r_plus algebraically.

A.title: Extremal RN throat as a local scaled limit
A.statement: In extremal RN m=|Q|>0 set r=m+lambda R and t=T/lambda. On compact subsets R>0, as positive lambda tends to zero the pulled-back metric converges with all derivatives to -(R^2/m^2)dT^2+(m^2/R^2)dR^2+m^2 gamma. This chart limit neither identifies the entire original exterior with a product nor proves a decoupled quantum theory.
A.proof_route: Substitute f=lambda^2 R^2/(m+lambda R)^2 and differentiate the rational coefficients on compact R-intervals bounded away from zero; use denominator lower bounds.

B.title: Limits near the horizon need a scale
B.statement: The unscaled subextremal exterior surface gravity tends to zero as Q^2 tends to m^2; a positive lower bound uniform in the full subextremal family is false.
B.proof_route: Use kappa=(r_plus-r_minus)/(2r_plus^2) and take Q^2 upward to m^2.

pairs.title: Linearized coupled equations and gauge identities

A.title: Linearized electrovacuum operator and gauge equivalence
A.statement: Fix a smooth exact oriented electrovacuum (g,F). A perturbation is a smooth symmetric tensor h and closed two-form f satisfying the first variation of Ric-Lambda g-2Q=0 and d star_g F=0. Gauge perturbations are (L_X g,L_X F); in a fixed potential sector f=d a, a also has a -> a+d chi. The symbol f here denotes a two-form, not the RN lapse.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Variation of the Hodge map and linearized Maxwell
A.statement: For a k-form omega, delta(star omega)=star(delta omega+(tr_g h/2)omega-h_sharp dot omega), where h_sharp acts in each covariant slot. Thus the Maxwell perturbation equation is d star[f+(tr h/2)F-h_sharp dot F]=0 and df=0.
A.proof_route: Differentiate inverse-metric components delta g^ab=-h^ab and volume delta vol=(tr h/2)vol in the alternating coordinate formula for star. Each raised covariant slot contributes one negative h_sharp term.

A.title: Pure gauge and parameter modes solve the linearized system
A.statement: For any smooth X the pair (L_Xg,L_XF) solves the linearized electrovacuum equations. A differentiable exact RN/KN parameter family yields additional parameter derivatives solving them. Gauge and parameter solutions are to be removed or retained according to boundary normalization before a decay claim is made.
A.proof_route: Differentiate naturality E(Phi_s^*g,Phi_s^*F)=Phi_s^*E(g,F)=0 along the local flow; differentiate E(g(p),F(p))=0 with fixed admitted chart and parameter domain.

A.title: Finite-slab linear perturbation estimate
A.statement: For the harmonic/field-strength linearization on a compact time slab whose slices are a three-torus, with smooth bounded coefficients and uniformly positive time matrix, the H^k perturbation energy is at most exp(C times absolute t) times its initial energy plus the Duhamel source norm, for integer k>=0. Zero initial subsidiary constraints remain zero.
A.proof_route: Differentiate the already checked symmetric first-order system, integrate by parts periodically and bound coefficient-derivative commutators. Complete the square for sources and integrate the scalar differential inequality. Differentiate the homogeneous subsidiary identities. This supplies a finite-time estimate only.

B.title: A stationary charge derivative does not decay away
B.statement: Differentiating RN with respect to its electric charge on a fixed exterior chart gives a nonradiating linearized solution with nonzero electric-flux variation. A theorem asserting decay of every component to zero without subtracting a parameter mode is false.
B.proof_route: Differentiate the flux q_e and the metric coefficients directly.

pairs.title: Energy currents and conditional stability estimates

A.title: Wave stress and multiplier currents
A.statement: For a real smooth scalar u on a smooth Lorentz domain solving Box_g u=V u+s with real smooth V, define T_ab=partial_a u partial_b u-(g_ab/2)(|du|^2+V u^2), J^X_a=T_ab X^b and K^X=T_ab nabla^(a X^b). Fluxes are integrals against oriented hypersurface volume or their null flux forms, with no unit null normal assumed.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Exact potential-wave multiplier identity
A.statement: The wave current satisfies div J^X=K^X+s X(u)-(X(V)/2)u^2. For a Killing X preserving V and s=0 it is divergence free. If X and the slice normal are future timelike and V>=0 then the corresponding future energy density is nonnegative.
A.proof_route: Expand nabla^a T_ab, commute scalar second derivatives and cancel the kinetic cross terms. The remainder is s partial_bu-(u^2/2)partial_b V. For positivity use an orthonormal rest frame and Cauchy–Schwarz.

A.title: Positive matrix-potential wave system energy
A.statement: Let U:R_t times R_x to R^N be smooth and sufficiently decaying to justify boundary limits, solving U_tt-U_xx+V(x)U=S with V smooth symmetric positive semidefinite. E(t)=one-half integral(|U_t|^2+|U_x|^2+U^T VU) obeys E_prime=integral U_t dot S and sqrt(E(t))<=sqrt(E(0))+2^-1/2 integral_0^t ||S||_2 for t>=0. Conservation by itself proves neither pointwise decay nor full coupled Einstein–Maxwell reconstruction.
A.proof_route: Multiply by U_t, integrate by parts, use symmetry and time independence of V. Cauchy–Schwarz gives E_prime<=sqrt(2E)||S||; regularize sqrt(E+delta) before integration and let delta decrease to zero.

A.title: An explicit conditional nonlinear energy closure
A.statement: If a nonnegative absolutely continuous energy satisfies E_prime<=C(1+t)^-1-delta E^(3/2) for delta>0 and E(0)>0 with C sqrt(E(0))<2delta, then E(t)<=E(0)[1-C sqrt(E(0))/(2delta)]^-2 on its existence interval. A separate continuation theorem is required for global existence.
A.proof_route: Differentiate E^-1/2 on positive intervals, integrate (1+t)^-1-delta, and pass through any zeros using E+eta or component intervals. This is an ODE implication, not a claim that RN/KN perturbations satisfy the premise.

B.title: A negative mode invalidates positive-energy stability
B.statement: If the self-adjoint spatial operator -partial_x^2+V has an L2 eigenfunction w with eigenvalue -sigma^2<0, U=exp(sigma t)w solves the homogeneous wave system and grows. Merely making V real symmetric does not exclude this.
B.proof_route: Substitute the eigenvalue equation. The example is conditional on the explicit eigenpair and requires no general spectral theorem.

pairs.title: Extremal horizon conservation and conditional derivative growth

A.title: Spherical scalar waves in regular extremal coordinates
A.statement: On the extremal RN ingoing domain v in R, r near or above m>0, take g=-D dv^2+2 dv dr+r^2 gamma with D=(1-m/r)^2. Let psi(v,r) be a real spherical C^3 solution of Box_g psi=0 and set phi=r psi. The scalar is a test field and does not source the metric.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Exact spherical horizon charge
A.statement: For such a scalar, H=partial_r phi(v,m) is independent of v. If H is nonzero, partial_r phi cannot tend to zero along the horizon.
A.proof_route: The reduced equation is 2phi_vr+partial_r(D phi_r)-(D_prime/r)phi=0. At r=m, D=D_prime=0, hence partial_v phi_r=0.

A.title: Second derivative growth under an explicit horizon decay hypothesis
A.statement: If the same solution is C^3 at the horizon, H is nonzero and phi(v,m) tends to zero as v tends to infinity, then partial_r^2 phi(v,m)/v tends to -H/m^2. Thus one transverse derivative grows linearly under these stated assumptions.
A.proof_route: Differentiate the reduced equation once in r and set r=m, using D_second(m)=2/m^2: partial_v phi_rr=-H/m^2+phi(v,m)/m^3. Integrate from a finite v0 and use the Cesaro implication from phi(v,m)->0. No decay theorem is used without being supplied.

B.title: Nonzero horizon charge alone does not force this growth
B.statement: A constant psi=c has phi=cr and H=c, while phi_rr=0; its horizon value phi(v,m)=cm does not decay and the derivative-growth hypothesis fails.
B.proof_route: Substitute phi=cr into the exact equation and evaluate horizon data.

pairs.title: Charged test-scalar scattering and superradiant flux

A.title: Massless charged scalar radial scattering problem
A.statement: On a fixed subextremal electric RN exterior choose A=-(Q/r)dt with A_t tending to zero at infinity and D_a=nabla_a-i e A_a. A real frequency omega>0 and spherical harmonic ell give psi=exp(-i omega t)Y_ell u(r)/r. Define r_star by dr_star/dr=f^-1 and fix a reference length L>0, put Theta=omega r_star-eQ log(r/L), and require u asymptotic to exp(-i Theta)+R exp(i Theta) at infinity and T exp(-i(omega-e Q/r_plus)r_star) at the future horizon, with errors o(1) in u and in its r_star derivative relative to these leading terms, and no other incoming horizon mode.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Charged radial equation and conserved Wronskian
A.statement: The massless charged wave equation D^aD_a psi=0 reduces to u_second+[(omega-eQ/r)^2-f(ell(ell+1)/r^2+f_prime/r)]u=0 in r_star. For real omega,e,Q the quantity Im(conjugate(u)u_prime) is constant.
A.proof_route: Expand the covariant derivative in the static chart, separate the sphere Laplacian, set phi=r psi and use partial_rstar=f partial_r. Multiply the real-coefficient ODE by conjugate(u) and take imaginary parts.

A.title: Exact scattering flux amplification criterion
A.statement: For a solution with the specified scattering asymptotics, |R|^2=1-[(omega-eQ/r_plus)/omega]|T|^2. If 0<omega<eQ/r_plus and T is nonzero, reflected flux exceeds incident flux. This is a conditional scattering identity, not an existence theorem for those asymptotics or an exponentially growing mode theorem.
A.proof_route: Evaluate the constant Wronskian at both ends; the oscillatory cross terms have zero imaginary contribution. The horizon coefficient is omega-e Phi_H in the gauge with zero potential at infinity.

B.title: Neutral spherical background scattering lacks charged amplification
B.statement: For e=0 and omega>0 the same identity gives |R|^2=1-|T|^2<=1. A nonzero black-hole charge alone does not give amplification for a neutral test scalar.

pairs.title: Connection sectors, holonomy and presymplectic boundaries

A.title: Differences of circle connections and fixed topology
A.statement: For two smooth normalized U(1) connections on the same principal circle bundle, local connection representatives differ by a global real one-form a on the base, their curvatures differ by da, and their curvature integrals on any closed oriented surface agree. Flat differences need not be gauge trivial.
A.proof_route: In overlapping trivializations the identical transition differential cancels between the representatives. Apply d and integrate da by Stokes on the closed surface. A gauge transformation has periods fixed by the chosen 2pi normalization; a closed a with different holonomy cannot be removed.

A.title: Fixed-background Maxwell presymplectic current
A.statement: For a fixed oriented background metric and two potential variations a1,a2 solving d star d a_i=0 on a fixed bundle sector, define the three-form omega(a1,a2)=a1 wedge star d a2-a2 wedge star d a1. Its integral over a specified spacelike hypersurface is the presymplectic pairing, when convergent. Overall action constants may be restored.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Closed current and gauge boundary term
A.statement: d omega=0 for the stated fixed-background variations. Replacing a1 by a1+d chi changes omega by d(chi star d a2), so gauge directions are degeneracies only with appropriate boundary/decay conditions. Metric variations of the full coupled theory require additional gravitational and mixed terms.
A.proof_route: Expand d omega by the graded Leibniz rule; da1 wedge star da2 equals da2 wedge star da1 by symmetry of the form pairing. The field equations remove the remaining terms. The gauge formula is one more Leibniz expansion.

A.title: Finite constrained mode quotient
A.statement: If a finite-dimensional truncation has symplectic space V and linear constraint space W with W^omega contained in W, then W/W^omega carries the descended nondegenerate form. This algebraic fact does not establish a smooth infinite-dimensional quotient of the Einstein–Maxwell solution space.
A.proof_route: Apply the exact published linear-algebra theorem after identifying V,W and checking coisotropy; retain all its finite-dimensional hypotheses.

B.title: Flat connection with nontrivial Wilson loop
B.statement: On S^1 times a contractible patch the connection a=theta dphi in a trivial circle bundle has zero curvature but holonomy exp(2pi i theta). It is gauge equivalent to zero precisely when theta is an integer in this normalization.
B.proof_route: Integrate around the circle; the periodic map exp(-i theta phi) exists exactly for integral theta.

pairs.title: Compatible discrete Maxwell constraints and finite algorithms

A.title: Finite cochain Maxwell phase space
A.statement: Fix finite real cochain spaces C0,C1,C2,C3 with matrices D0,D1,D2 satisfying D1D0=0 and D2D1=0, and symmetric positive definite matrices M1,M2. Let magnetic b lie in C2 and electric displacement d in the dual of C1, with evolution b_dot=-D1 M1^-1 d and d_dot=D1^T M2 b. Discrete constraints are D2 b and D0^T d.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Finite compatible leapfrog evolution
A.statement: Inputs are these finite matrices, initial b_0,d_half and a positive step h and nonnegative integer N. For n=0,...,N-1 set b_next=b-h D1 M1^-1 d; then d_next=d+h D1^T M2 b_next; record the new pair. Output is the N+1 states. Inverses are computed once by exact Gaussian elimination for rational positive definite input or by a separately specified numerical linear solve.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Exact discrete constraints and semidiscrete energy
A.statement: Every exact-arithmetic update preserves D2 b and D0^T d. The continuous semidiscrete energy (b^T M2 b+d^T M1^-1 d)/2 is conserved. The staggered update conserves (b^T M2 b+d^T M1^-1 d-h b^T M2 D1 M1^-1 d)/2, which is positive definite if h times the largest singular value of M2^(1/2) D1 M1^-1/2 is less than 2.
A.proof_route: Apply D2 and D0^T to the updates and use the two complex identities. Differentiate the continuous energy and cancel transposes. For the staggered invariant expand the quadratic in the two updates; positivity follows by bounding the cross term by h sigma ||M2^1/2 b|| ||M1^-1/2 d|| and completing squares.

A.title: Finite arithmetic termination and cost
A.statement: For rational admissible matrices and finite N, the update terminates after finitely many rational operations. Dense elimination uses O(n1^3) arithmetic operations and each dense step O(n1 n2+n1^2+n2^2), with storage bounded by the matrices and recorded finite states. These are arithmetic counts, not bounded bit complexity or floating point accuracy guarantees.
A.proof_route: Each elimination pivot is nonzero for the positive definite solve under a fixed no-pivot Cholesky-free elimination schedule; enumerate finite row operations, matrix-vector products and N loops. Rational coefficient bit growth is separately unbounded by this arithmetic count.

B.title: Constraint preservation does not imply stable evolution
B.statement: For a single oscillatory mode with step h sigma>2, the two-by-two leapfrog map has trace 2-h^2 sigma^2<-2 and determinant one, hence an eigenvalue of magnitude greater than one. Gauss constraints can still be exactly preserved.
B.proof_route: Write the update matrix [[1,-h sigma],[h sigma,1-h^2 sigma^2]] and solve its characteristic polynomial.

pairs.title: Effective nonlinear electromagnetism and semiclassical consistency

A.title: A smooth nonlinear electromagnetic constitutive model
A.statement: On an oriented Lorentz four-manifold and fixed bundle sector put X=-F_ab F^ab/4, Y=-F_ab(star F)^ab/4 and L=L(X,Y), a C^2 real function. Define H^{ab}=L_X F^{ab}+L_Y(star F)^{ab}. Adopt stationarity of integral L vol under compactly supported connection variations, with source coupling supplied independently. No quantum origin is included in this definition.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Constitutive field equation from compact variations
A.statement: For source-free compact variations on the fixed metric, stationarity implies nabla_a H^{ab}=0 together with dF=0. In particular L=X+alpha X^2+beta Y^2 gives H=(1+2alpha X)F+2beta Y star F. Hyperbolicity of this nonlinear model is not a consequence of this variation.
A.proof_route: Use delta X=-F^ab delta F_ab/2 and delta Y=-(star F)^ab delta F_ab/2 at fixed metric, substitute delta F=2nabla_[a delta A_b], and integrate by parts with compact support.

A.title: Conditional semiclassical Einstein–Maxwell source contract
A.statement: A semiclassical candidate consists of a smooth classical g,F and specified renormalized source assignments T_ren[g,F,state], j_ren[g,F,state] on a chosen state class. Require nabla_a j_ren^a=0 and nabla^a T_ren,ab=F_bc j_ren^c in the inherited sign convention. These Ward/exchange identities and state dependence are part of an admitted interface, not a construction of the assignments or proof of the semiclassical equations.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Necessary Ward consistency of coupled sources
A.statement: If the coupled equations with classical Maxwell stress and sources T_ren,j_ren hold at sufficient differentiability and Lambda is constant, then charge conservation and the exchange identity are necessary. Neither identity is sufficient for a quantum state, a renormalized stress construction or a well-posed semiclassical evolution.
A.proof_route: Take a divergence of Maxwell and use the antisymmetric curvature contraction to obtain current conservation. Take the divergence of Einstein, use contracted Bianchi and the inherited Maxwell stress divergence, and rearrange.

B.title: Small invariants do not alone control derivative corrections
B.statement: A small-amplitude rapidly oscillating smooth field can have small X,Y while its derivatives are arbitrarily large. Therefore inequalities on alpha X and beta Y alone do not validate a derivative-truncated electromagnetic effective action.
B.proof_route: On a fixed chart take a smooth field profile scaled in amplitude by epsilon and in wavelength by epsilon^2; first derivatives scale as epsilon^-1 while quadratic field invariants scale as epsilon^2.

pairs.title: Reduced stationary uniqueness and explicit research boundaries

A.title: Positive matrix harmonic-map boundary problem
A.statement: Let Omega be a bounded connected smooth Euclidean domain and let Phi_i be smooth maps on its closure into positive definite Hermitian n-by-n matrices with determinant one. Put J_i=Phi_i^-1 d Phi_i and assume div J_i=0. Require the two maps to agree on the entire boundary. This is an abstract Riemannian target comparison problem, not a spacetime uniqueness theorem.
A.proof_route: Definition fixes exactly the data, equivalence and admissibility conditions stated; existence is a separate obligation.

A.title: Positive-matrix comparison identity
A.statement: With Psi=Phi_1 Phi_0^-1-I and Delta J=J_1-J_0, the comparison identity is Delta tr(Psi)=sum_a tr((Delta J_a)^dagger Phi_1 Delta J_a Phi_0^-1)>=0. Consequently identical Dirichlet data force Phi_1=Phi_0 on Omega.
A.proof_route: Differentiate d Phi=Phi J, d Phi^-1=-J Phi^-1 and div J=0 to obtain the displayed trace identity; use J_i^dagger=Phi_i J_i Phi_i^-1 to rewrite it as a Hilbert–Schmidt square. Since det(Phi_1 Phi_0^-1)=1 and its eigenvalues are positive, trace>=n by finite AM–GM. The maximum principle with zero boundary trace then gives trace=n, and all eigenvalues equal one imply equality of the Hermitian positive matrices.

A.title: What remains before a Kerr–Newman uniqueness theorem
A.statement: Transferring matrix comparison to stationary electrovacuum requires symmetry inheritance, commuting stationary/axial Killing fields, circularity, a global orbit-space theorem, well-defined Ernst/twist potentials, the correct target and positive representation, and controlled axis/horizon/asymptotic boundary terms. Analyticity, horizon regularity, connectedness and nondegeneracy assumptions must match the selected theorem. None is silently inferred from stationarity.
A.proof_route: Nonlogical roadmap only. Read CCH Sections 2–3,6–8 in full and the primary theorem proof before adding any spacetime uniqueness theorem as a supplier. The present bounded-domain matrix theorem has an independent proof route.

B.title: A scalar diagonal sector
B.statement: For n=2, Phi=diag(exp(u),exp(-u)) satisfies div(Phi^-1 dPhi)=0 exactly when Delta u=0. Two such maps with identical full Dirichlet data agree.
B.proof_route: Compute J=diag(du,-du) and apply the scalar harmonic uniqueness proof.

A.title: Independently adopted charged test-scalar regime
A.statement: For this model a classical complex scalar of specified charge coupling propagates by D^aD_a psi=0 on a specified fixed subextremal or extremal RN background, with its stress and current omitted from the background equations. This is a test-field model; field amplitude, wavelength, boundary preparation and observation interval must be specified before comparing with physical data.
A.proof_route: Physical formulation and source/scope review are required; no proof of applicability is asserted. The inherited test-model item supplies the distinction between prescribed background and coupled field.

A.title: Conditional charged-wave flux consequence
A.statement: Within the adopted test-scalar model, a real-frequency scattering solution with the precise two-end asymptotics and nonzero transmission has reflected energy flux greater than incident flux in the band 0<omega<e Phi_H. This conditional consequence concerns that model and specified gauge-normalized flux, not a measured astrophysical extraction efficiency.
A.proof_route: Apply the mathematical Wronskian identity and the physical model assignment; identify flux ratios from the normalized mode amplitudes.

A.title: Selected effective classical constitutive adoption
A.statement: An effective-model use specifies a particular C^2 L(X,Y), its dimensionful coefficients and a domain where it is adopted as the constitutive law. Claims of low-energy quantum derivation, coefficient matching, errors, or semiclassical backreaction require separate QFT suppliers and cannot be inferred from formal variation.
A.proof_route: Source/scope review is owed before authoring the physical postulate. It adopts an explicit classical model, not a quantum existence theorem.

B.title: Why a small test amplitude needs an interval-dependent bound
B.statement: If a background approximation has forcing residual bounded by C epsilon^2 and a separately established perturbation estimate bounds solution difference by K(T) times the integrated residual on [0,T], then the error is at most K(T) C T epsilon^2 in the specified norm. This conditional implication does not provide the required nonlinear perturbation estimate or justify T tending to infinity.
B.proof_route: Integrate the residual bound and apply the explicitly assumed error estimate; its norm and K(T) are part of the hypothesis, not an invented theorem.
